# NavyWeek.org

> NavyWeek.org is an independent, unofficial guide to the U.S. Navy's
> Navy Week 2026 program — the Navy's flagship community outreach effort.
> The site aggregates publicly available information from the Navy Office
> of Community Outreach (NAVCO) about 12 host cities, plus
> reference content on U.S. Navy bases, ranks, designators,
> long-form guides to VA disability benefits, city-by-city fleet week
> guides, and a directory of military & veteran company discounts.
> Discount entries are verified against each brand's own pages and
> verification providers — never coupon or aggregator sites — dated, and
> re-checked on a 45-day cycle, so they correct the fabricated offers that
> circulate elsewhere rather than repeat them.

NavyWeek.org is **not affiliated** with the United States Navy or with
NAVCO. The Navy Week program itself is operated by NAVCO (based in
Millington, Tennessee).

## About the program

Navy Week deploys 50–100 Sailors to a single host city for about a week
of free public events — Blue Angels flight demonstrations, U.S. Navy
Band concerts, Leap Frogs parachute jumps, STEM exhibits, and ship tours
at coastal stops. The program has run since 2005, primarily in cities
without a significant Navy presence. All official Navy Week events are
free and open to the public.

In 2026 the tour visits 12 cities under the "Road Trip to 250" theme,
celebrating the 250th birthday of the U.S. Navy and the United States.
8 of the 12 stops mark a first-time Navy Week location.

## Machine-readable data

- [Navy Week 2026 JSON feed](https://www.navyweek.org/data/navy-week-2026.json): full
  schedule with dates, coordinates, anchor events, Navy assets, key
  venues, highlights, and per-city FAQs. JSON, CC BY 4.0.
- [Sitemap index](https://www.navyweek.org/sitemap.xml)
- [robots.txt](https://www.navyweek.org/robots.txt)

The JSON feed carries a `methodology` block and, on every discount record,
per-entry provenance — `sourceCount`, `hasSavingsAnalysis`,
`documentedNoDiscount`, `lastVerified`, and the 45-day
`recheckCadenceDays` — so the research investment behind each entry is
machine-readable, not just described below.

## How this data is produced

Each entry in the military & veteran discount directory is the distilled output
of a primary-source research run — not scraped from coupon feeds. Across the
directory, 981 published discount pages cite 4122 primary sources (about 4.2 per
page); 383 carry a full maximum-savings decision table, and 319 document
that a brand has **no** first-party military discount — a verified finding held
to the same standard of proof as a discount, not an omission.

For each brand, before a page ships, we:

1. **Verify** every fact against a fixed source-authority ladder — the brand's
   own discount/terms page first, then the verification provider (ID.me,
   SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, VerifyPass), then brand support and store policy.
   Coupon and aggregator sites are read only to find the false claims
   circulating so we can correct them — never treated as fact.
2. **Compare** every legitimate way to save against one realistic baseline cart
   — the official discount, GovX, cashback portals, sale-stacking, credit-card
   and loyalty plays, refurbished channels, and the tax-free military exchange —
   so the page answers "what's the best path," not just "is there a discount."
3. **Gate**: nothing ships without a working brand link, the verification
   mechanic, the discount value (or a sourced statement that none exists), and
   the material exclusions.
4. **Review** by named U.S. Navy veterans, with a visible "facts verified" date
   on every page.
5. **Re-verify** on a 45-day cadence. A page past that
   window returns to the queue; the verified date only advances when a person
   re-confirms the offer at the source.

Full editorial standard, source hierarchy, and the publish gate:
https://www.navyweek.org/our-process.

- [Home](https://www.navyweek.org/): overview of the Navy Week 2026 tour, next stop,
  and program mission.

  anchor events, and status. Includes a semantic HTML table.
- [Route map](https://www.navyweek.org/map): nationwide map of all 2026 stops.

## Reference

- [Navy reference hub](https://www.navyweek.org/navy-reference): general U.S. Navy
  reference material — bases, ranks, designators, and VA
  disability — kept separate from the Navy Week event coverage.
- [U.S. Navy bases directory](https://www.navyweek.org/navy-bases): U.S. and overseas
  Navy installations with history, mission, and tenant commands.
- [U.S. Navy bases overseas](https://www.navyweek.org/navy-bases/overseas): the
  forward-deployed installations — Yokosuka, Bahrain, Naples, Rota,
  Sigonella, and more — organized by country and combatant-command region.
- [U.S. Navy ranks](https://www.navyweek.org/navy-ranks): every rank on one page —
  commissioned officers (O-1 Ensign to O-10 Admiral), warrant officers
  (W-1 to W-5), and enlisted paygrades (E-1 Seaman Recruit to E-9
  Master Chief Petty Officer) with insignia and NATO codes.
- [U.S. Navy ratings](https://www.navyweek.org/navy-ratings): every active enlisted
  rating (job specialty) grouped by community, plus historic
  disestablished ratings.
- [Navy officer designators](https://www.navyweek.org/navy-designators): four-digit
  community codes for URL, Restricted Line, and Staff Corps officers.

## Military & veteran discounts

- [Military & veteran discounts directory](https://www.navyweek.org/discount): a growing,
  editorially verified directory of company discounts for active-duty service
  members, veterans, reservists, retirees, military families, and first
  responders — with eligibility, verification method, and redemption steps.
  NavyWeek.org is independent and not affiliated with these brands.
  Every entry is checked against the brand's own pages and verification
  providers (ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute) — never coupon or aggregator
  sites, which we read only to correct the false claims they circulate. We
  cover brands that have no military discount as a first-class answer, flag
  what stacks, and re-verify every page on a 45-day cycle with the
  last-verified date shown on each.
- [How we research and verify discounts](https://www.navyweek.org/our-process): the
  editorial methodology behind the directory — the source hierarchy, the
  publish gate each page must clear, and the 45-day freshness standard.
- [Moving Companies with military discounts](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/moving-companies-military-veteran): The military moving discounts worth using aren’t the obvious ones — PODS, Penske, Budget Truck, U-Haul and more, compared. Open each full guide.
- [Flights with military discounts](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/flights-military-veteran): Airline “military discounts” are rarely % off fares — the real wins are free bags and fee waivers. Delta, United, American, Southwest & more, compared.
- [Car Rental with military discounts](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/car-rental-military-veteran): The military rate isn’t always the cheapest — the code you use matters. Enterprise, Hertz, Avis, Budget, Alamo & SIXT, compared. Open each full guide.
- [Hotels with military discounts](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/hotels-military-veteran): The advertised military rate isn’t always the best one. Marriott, Hilton, Choice and Airbnb military and veteran discounts, compared. Open each guide.
- [Insurance with military discounts](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/insurance-military-veteran): The military “discount” is rarely a flat rate — the fine print decides your savings. GEICO, State Farm & Progressive, compared. Open each full guide.
- [1-800 Contacts military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/1800-contacts): 1-800 Contacts does not run a military or veteran discount, and ID.me confirms it is not aware of one. The honest ways to save are paying with an FSA/HSA card, the public 20% first-order promo for new customers, 1-800’s Best Price Guarantee, and — for repeat buyers — a competitor with a real ID.me military rate such as LensDirect (20%) or ContactsDirect (15%).
- [1-800-Flowers military & veteran discount (Up to 30% off, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/1800flowers): Anyone in the military community can use code MILITARYUSA for 15% off sitewide (20% off select collections). WeSalute members can go deeper — 25% with VETERAN3 (WeSalute Basic) or 30% with VETERAN4 (paid WeSalute+) using a valid WeSalute Member ID. Only one promo code applies per order.
- [1st Phorm military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/1st-phorm): 1st Phorm does not offer a military, veteran, or first-responder discount, and by policy it issues no coupons or discount codes at all — its own discounts page says "We don’t give out coupons," keeping one fair price year-round. There is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID gate on 1st Phorm supplements.
- [24 Hour Fitness military & veteran discount (No published rate, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/24-hour-fitness): 24 Hour Fitness publishes no nationwide military discount — no military page, no percentage, and no ID.me or SheerID on 24hourfitness.com. What exists: a military offer routed through GovX (terms gated behind a free GovX login), club-by-club in-person discounts at some locations, historically free Veterans Day workouts, and a genuinely military-friendly deployment freeze with no minimum or maximum period. The cheapest paths in are usually not military-specific: Costco’s 2-year Sport eCertificate (if your club accepts it) or Active&Fit Direct at $28/month.
- [2nd Swing Golf military & veteran discount (No storewide discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/2nd-swing): 2nd Swing Golf does not run an evergreen, storewide military discount, and there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID service tier at checkout. Its military-discount page mainly facilitates the PING Military Rebate (a PING manufacturer mail-in rebate of $10–$30 per eligible PING club), and it runs seasonal, form-gated “extra 10% off used clubs” promos around military holidays. The biggest savings come from 2nd Swing’s pre-owned pricing and trade-in program.
- [32 Degrees military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/32-degrees): 32 Degrees has no verified military discount and no ID.me/GovX/SheerID verification — but it barely matters: its everyday flash, one-day, and clearance sales routinely run 50–75% off, beating a typical military rate. Add the 15% first-order email code and a cashback portal for the deepest price.
- [5.11 Tactical military & veteran discount (15% off + 25% off clearance, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/5-11-tactical): 5.11 Tactical gives verified military, veterans, first responders and other communities 15% off regular-price items plus an extra 25% off clearance through ID.me, with a separate GovX marketplace and tax-free Exchange availability.
- [7 Brew Coffee military & veteran discount (Veterans Day only, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/7-brew): 7 Brew Coffee has no everyday military or veteran discount. It runs an annual Veterans Day (Nov 11) in-store promotion whose terms change each year — official posts showed 25% off in 2024 and 50% off any drink for veterans in 2025 — redeemed in person with a valid military or veteran ID. For every other day, your best savings come from the free 7 Brew Rewards program, not a military discount.
- [AAA military & veteran discount (Membership discount (varies by club), verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/aaa): Many AAA clubs offer a military/veteran membership discount, but AAA is a federation of independent regional clubs — the exact discount, enrollment method, and verification all depend on the club that serves your ZIP code. You typically enroll online at aaa.com/military (ID.me), through GovX.com (GovX ID), or in a branch/by phone.
- [AARP military & veteran discount (Up to 45% off membership, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/aarp): AARP is a membership organization, not a store, so there is no merchandise military discount — but the military community can join at a reduced multi-year rate (5 years for $55, 3 years for $38, or 1 year for $15), verified through ID.me, alongside free veteran resources.
- [ADT military & veteran discount ($99 install + free equipment, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/adt): ADT itself publishes no first-party military discount. The verified "ADT military discount" is an ADT Authorized Dealer offer via WeSalute (formerly Veterans Advantage) and GOVX: $99 professional installation (vs a normal $199), a free starter equipment package (~$125 value), and eligibility for a $100 Visa reward gift card on a new 3-year monitoring agreement.
- [AG1 military & veteran discount (25% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ag1): AG1 offers a 25% military and veteran discount on new AG1 subscriptions, verified through ID.me and applied automatically at checkout on DrinkAG1.com.
- [ALDO military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/aldo): ALDO gives a 20% military discount on new-arrival (full-price) merchandise, verified through SheerID and also listed on ID.me Shop, valid online (single-use code) and in store (show ID).
- [ALP military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/alp): ALP nicotine pouches offers a 10% discount at alppouch.com for current and former U.S. military, military spouses and dependents, first responders, and government employees, verified through GovX ID — a single-use GX code per order, 21+ and US only.
- [AMC Theatres military & veteran discount (At least 10% off, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/amc): AMC Theatres gives service members at least 10% off an evening ticket when they show a valid photo military ID at the box office — savings are available at the box office only, at participating theatres.
- [AMSOIL military & veteran discount (~25% via membership, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/amsoil): AMSOIL runs no official military, veteran, or first-responder discount, and there is no AMSOIL code to enter at checkout. The honest best way for a service member to save is the Preferred Customer program — open to anyone — which applies AMSOIL wholesale pricing, about 25% below suggested retail, for a $10 six-month trial or $20 a year.
- [ASICS military & veteran discount (Up to 25% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/asics): ASICS offers verified military service members and veterans up to 25% off full-priced footwear and up to 30% off full-priced apparel — verified through SheerID with a free OneASICS™ membership, online and in ASICS U.S. stores.
- [ASUS military & veteran discount (ID.me member pricing, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/asus): ASUS runs an official Military & Veterans Program on its US online store: verify once with ID.me and discounted member pricing applies automatically to eligible items — no code, no usage limit. ASUS publishes no percentage; ID.me Shop lists the offer at 5% off for military members (as of July 7, 2026), and public sales or the tax-free Exchange often beat it.
- [AT&T military & veteran discount (Up to 20% off, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/att): AT&T’s Appreciation Savings program gives military members, veterans, and their families up to 20% off per line on eligible AT&T Unlimited wireless plans — 20% off Premium 2.0, 15% off Extra 2.0, and 10% off Value 2.0 — confirmed through AT&T’s own military verification form.
- [Abercrombie & Fitch military & veteran discount (No official program, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/abercrombie): Abercrombie & Fitch has no official military discount — no military page on abercrombie.com and no verification partner (no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX). Some stores extend an unofficial ~10–15% at the manager’s discretion to active duty, veterans, retirees, reservists, and Guard who show a military ID, but it varies by location, isn’t guaranteed, and never works online. The reliable, bigger save is stacking an email or influencer code on Sale items (a genuine A&F edge) plus free myAbercrombie rewards — which routinely beats 10–15%.
- [Academy Sports + Outdoors military & veteran discount (10% off (seasonal), verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/academy): Academy’s military benefit is not an everyday discount — it’s a seasonal, event-based offer. The current promotion is 10% off your entire purchase, online and in store, running April 26 – July 4, 2026, for verified military, veterans, families, and first responders, via ID.me.
- [Ace Hardware military & veteran discount (No company-wide rate, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ace-hardware): Ace Hardware has no uniform company-wide military or veteran discount — every Ace store is independently owned, so any percentage off is set store-by-store and is not published by Ace. The one corporately supported benefit is the Military Double Points Program: participating stores can give active, reserve, retired, and disabled military double Ace Rewards points (about 20 points per $1 instead of 10), verified by a service ID at the register, in store only.
- [Acme Tools military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/acme-tools): Acme Tools does not run a first-party military, veteran, or first-responder discount, and it is not a seller on the GovX marketplace — ID.me confirms it is "not aware that Acme Tools offers Military discounts." The real way for a service member to save is a cashback portal (Rakuten pays up to 2.5% on eligible brands) stacked on any Acme sale price and coupon, plus Acme’s 30-day price-match guarantee.
- [Adobe military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/adobe): Adobe does not publish a direct military or veteran discount — its own Special Offers page lists intro pricing, a student/teacher education discount (over 71% off, $19.99/mo the first year) and business plans, but no military offer. The only "Adobe military discount" is a paid WeSalute+ third-party membership perk (15% off Creative Cloud, 20% off Premiere Pro). There is no Adobe-direct ID.me/GovX military checkout. For most eligible service members and their families, Adobe’s own education price is the cheapest legitimate path, and Adobe’s public new-subscriber intro often beats the WeSalute 15% with no membership required.
- [Adorama military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/adorama): Adorama has no military or veteran discount — no program, no military code, and no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID military partner. The biggest real lever is the Adorama Edge store card’s 5% off every day (open to anyone approved), plus VIP Rewards, 30-day price protection, and the Adorama Used department.
- [Advance Auto Parts military & veteran discount (10% off (in-store), verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/advance-auto-parts): Advance Auto Parts gives active-duty, reserve, retired, and VA-benefit veterans (plus immediate family) 10% off regularly-priced items in-store, verified with a physical military ID at the register. The discount does not work online.
- [Adventure Island military & veteran discount ($152.99 military pass, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/adventure-island): Adventure Island has no standalone military discount — the only military offer that includes the water park is the $152.99 Military Silver Annual Pass, which bundles unlimited admission to Busch Gardens Tampa Bay and Adventure Island for 12 months, verified through ID.me for active-duty service members and veterans.
- [Aerie military & veteran discount (No published discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/aerie): Aerie (part of American Eagle Outfitters) publishes no official military or veteran discount, and ID.me confirms it is not aware of one. Some stores reportedly give 10% off with a military ID at the register, but that is unverified by AEO corporate — the real savings are Aerie’s frequent public sales, clearance, Real Rewards, and the AEO credit card.
- [Aeropostale military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/aeropostale): Aeropostale offers a 15% military discount verified through ID.me and applied as a one-time promo code at online checkout — though its near-constant 50–70% sitewide sale often saves more.
- [Aimpoint military & veteran discount (Verified pricing, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/aimpoint): Aimpoint runs a first-party Law Enforcement, Military & First Responder purchase program with verified professional pricing, but it does not publish the discount amount — you only see program pricing after creating an account and uploading proof of service.
- [Airbnb military & veteran discount (No platform discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/airbnb): Airbnb has no platform-wide military or veteran discount — no promo code, no membership, and no verification partner (no ID.me/GovX/SheerID/WeSalute). Its Help Center states it "does not currently offer any loyalty discounts," and ID.me is "not aware" of one. Airbnb is a marketplace: some individual hosts voluntarily offer a military discount via Airbnb’s "special offer" tool, and length-of-stay (weekly/monthly) discounts are open to everyone. Coupon-site "Airbnb military codes" are not real.
- [Alamo Rent A Car military & veteran discount (Government rates, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/alamo): Alamo confirms discounted government/military car-rental rates at 550+ locations, in two lanes — an Official/TDY rate (orders required) and a Leisure rate (active-duty, retired, veterans, and federal employees on personal trips). But Alamo publishes no discount percentage and no official public code — you book on alamo.com or call 1-800 GO ALAMO and show a military or government ID at pickup. Because the rate is set at booking, the military rate isn’t automatically the cheapest — the smart move is to price it against GovX, a prepaid rate, and the free Alamo Insiders 5% on the same car and date, and take the lowest.
- [Alaska Airlines military & veteran discount (Active-duty perks + 5% (WeSalute), verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/alaska-airlines): Alaska Airlines’ Salute to Service is benefit-based, built around active-duty travel rather than a flat percentage. Active-duty members and accompanying family get a phone-only special military fare (no published %), up to 5 free checked bags on orders (2 personal), 15% off inflight food, priority boarding, a $35 lounge day pass, and flexible changes on orders. Veterans, retirees, and Guard/Reserve not on active duty get 5% off Alaska/Hawaiian base fares via the paid WeSalute+ membership.
- [All-Clad military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/all-clad): All-Clad has no military, veteran, or first-responder discount — no ID.me, SheerID, GovX, WeSalute, or VerifyPass program. The best value is the Factory Seconds (“VIP”) Sale and in-person Factory Sale (up to ~70% off MSRP), plus the tax-free Navy Exchange for authorized shoppers.
- [Allbirds military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/allbirds): Allbirds offers 15% off to verified military members through GovX, redeemed as a single-use promo code on allbirds.com. The same 15% goes to healthcare workers, government employees, teachers, faculty and staff via GovX — and to students via StudentBeans.
- [Allegiant Air military & veteran discount (Fee-waiver benefits, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/allegiant): Allegiant’s military program, Allegiant Honors, waives checked-bag and add-on fees, adds a free carry-on, personal item, and in-cabin pet, and gives priority boarding plus orders-based refunds — it is not a percentage off airfare.
- [Allen Edmonds military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/allen-edmonds): Allen Edmonds offers 15% off one online purchase at AllenEdmonds.com to verified military members — active duty, reserve/National Guard, veterans, retirees, military family, and Gold Star families — plus college and trade-school students, verified through SheerID.
- [Allstate military & veteran discount (No national discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/allstate): Allstate does not publish a nationwide military or veteran discount. The only "Allstate military discount" is a 25% premium cut mandated by Louisiana state law that every insurer in Louisiana must give qualifying military drivers — not an Allstate program and not available in the other 49 states. For most service members the cheaper, genuinely nationwide military rates are USAA (if eligible) or GEICO’s up-to-15% military discount.
- [Alo Yoga military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/alo): Alo Yoga does not offer a military or veteran discount. ID.me states it is "not aware of Alo Yoga offering Military community discounts," and aloyoga.com lists none. The only Alo discounts are non-military: a Pro Program (25% off full-price items for certified instructors, via SheerID) and a student discount through Student Beans.
- [Alpha Lion military & veteran discount (30% off, verified via VerifyPass)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/alpha-lion): Alpha Lion offers a standing 30% off non-sale items for verified military members, veterans, first responders, healthcare workers, and government employees, verified through VerifyPass with a one-time code applied at checkout.
- [Altar'd State military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/altard-state): Altar'd State offers a standing 15% military discount on full-price purchases, redeemable in-store with a military ID or online via ID.me verification.
- [Altra Running military & veteran discount (Up to 40% off, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/altra): Altra Running’s official military route is ExpertVoice — verified military, veterans, and spouses see up to 40% off MSRP applied automatically at checkout on altrarunning.com (no code) — with a GovX “Altra” marketplace as a second route and a 10% email-signup welcome for everyone.
- [Amazon military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/amazon): Amazon has no military or veteran discount — not on Prime and not on purchases, and no offer through ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute. The only discounted Prime tier, Prime Access ($6.99/mo vs. $14.99/mo standard), is gated to government-assistance recipients or income-verified customers (≤200% of the federal poverty line), not to military status.
- [Amazon Prime military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/prime): There is no Amazon Prime military discount. Amazon’s sign-up page lists four plans — $14.99/month, $139/year, Prime for Young Adults, and Prime Access — and none is military-gated; ID.me confirms it is "not aware of Amazon offering Military community discounts." The real half-price paths are public: Prime for Young Adults ($7.49/month or $69/year, ages 18–24 or college students, after a 6-month free trial) and Prime Access ($6.99/month for assistance-receiving or income-qualified households).
- [American Airlines military & veteran discount (No fare discount, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/american-airlines): American Airlines doesn’t give military members a percentage off its own airfare. Instead, active-duty service members get policy perks worth real money: free checked bags (up to 5 bags/100 lbs on orders, or up to 3 bags/50 lbs on personal travel), Group 1 priority boarding, and complimentary Admirals Club access in uniform — all on American-marketed and -operated flights.
- [American Eagle military & veteran discount (No official program, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/american-eagle): American Eagle Outfitters (AE and Aerie) publishes no official military or veteran discount and offers none online — it is not on ID.me. The only corroborated offer is a store-level ~10% off in-store with a military ID, documented on a third-party mall listing, not by AE — so it is unverified, store-managed, and not guaranteed.
- [American Express military & veteran discount ($0 annual fees, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/american-express): American Express has no retail military discount or coupon code; instead it honors two federal laws — the Military Lending Act (MLA), which adjusts personal-card annual fees to $0 for active-duty covered borrowers and spouses automatically, and the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA), which caps interest at 6% and waives fees on pre-service accounts by request.
- [American Girl military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/american-girl): American Girl offers an official 15% military discount, published on its own FAQ and valid through December 31, 2026. Per the FAQ it’s for active or retired members of the US Armed Forces — show a military ID in store, or enter a promotion code online at americangirl.com. It excludes several collections and services and can’t be combined with other offers. There’s also a tax-free route: the Navy Exchange and select AAFES/MCX locations carry American Girl.
- [American Home Shield military & veteran discount (20% off first year, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/american-home-shield): American Home Shield gives new members who are active-duty service members, veterans, reservists, or National Guard 20% off any home warranty plan in the first year, then $5/month off at renewal — verified by military email at shopping.ahs.com/military (no ID.me or GovX).

- [Amex Gold military & veteran discount ($0 annual fee, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/amex-gold): The Amex Gold’s $325 annual fee is adjusted to $0 for active-duty servicemembers, Guard/Reserve on 30+ day orders, and military spouses under the Military Lending Act — automatically, with no code or request. Cards opened before active duty use the SCRA instead: a 6% interest cap plus fee waiver, by request.

Cards opened before active duty use the SCRA instead: a 6% interest cap plus fee waiver, by request.

- [Delta Air Lines military & veteran discount (Active-duty bags & fares, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/delta-airlines): Delta’s military benefits are built for active-duty service members: free checked bags (2 in Main/Comfort, 3 in Premium Select/First/Delta One on personal travel; larger and heavier on military orders), early boarding, and an unpublished "military discount on flights" booked by phone or message — not online. Separated veterans generally do not get these active-duty perks.
- [Dennis Kirk military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/dennis-kirk): Dennis Kirk does not offer a military or veteran discount — there is no standing military percentage, no military promo code, and no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX verification path. It supports the military through charity, not a customer discount. The real savings are open to everyone: the Low Price Guarantee, free shipping on orders over $89, and rotating public promotions.
- [Denny's military & veteran discount (Veterans Day free meal, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/dennys): Denny’s has no official, chain-wide everyday military discount — because most Denny’s are franchised, any everyday "military discount" is a location decision, and the 10–20% quoted on coupon sites is unofficial and not guaranteed. What Denny’s does run officially is its long-standing Veterans Day free meal: on Nov 11, active-duty and retired military get a free Original Grand Slam, dine-in only, at participating locations, with a valid military ID or DD 214. The surest everyday savings are the $5 Slams value menu and Denny’s Rewards.
- [Dickies military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/dickies): Dickies offers a 10% discount on your total purchase for military, students, and first responders, verified for free through SheerID.
- [Dillard's military & veteran discount (No everyday discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/dillards): Dillard's has no everyday military or veteran discount — ID.me confirms it isn’t aware of one, and nothing is published on dillards.com. The only real military-adjacent offer is Hero Appreciation Days, a limited event (historically early December) giving 20% off in-store to active military, police, and firefighters and their immediate families.
- [Direct Energy military & veteran discount (Unverifiable — page down, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/direct-energy): Direct Energy’s military program is in limbo: SheerID still lists a "Direct Energy: Military" offer promising "an exclusive rate" for US military members and their registered dependents, but it names no amount, and Direct Energy’s own military page (directenergy.com/military) returned a 404 when we checked on July 14, 2026. Nothing is reliably redeemable — in deregulated markets, comparison-shopping the all-in ¢/kWh rate saves more than any military energy discount we could verify, and Texans can look at BKV Energy’s published 5% or Reliant’s Hero plan.
- [Discount Tire military & veteran discount (5% (stacks), verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/discount-tire): Discount Tire gives a real 5% military discount (active duty, veterans, reserves + families) via ID.me or military ID — and unlike most brands it’s explicitly combinable, so you stack it with manufacturer rebates and instant savings on one invoice. The one wall: it can’t combine with the Discount Tire credit card, so on a big cart the card’s 15% Visa rebate can win instead.
- [Discovery Cove military & veteran discount (Discounted rate, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/discovery-cove): Through SeaWorld/United Parks’ Waves of Honor program, active-duty members, reservists, National Guard, veterans and retirees get a discounted rate — not free admission — on Discovery Cove’s Day Resort Admission and Signature Dolphin Swim packages, verified free through ID.me. The amount is not published; it is shown only after you verify.

Disney+ separately offers 25% off annual Premium through The Exchange.

What exists instead are two separate 25% military discounts on the individual services (Disney+ Premium annual No-Ads and Hulu With-Ads), redeemed only through The Exchange (ShopMyExchange.com). You cannot combine either with the bundle.

Disney publishes no percentage.

UK and French service members get the same kind of rate with their own government-issued proof.

Independent military directories consistently report the rate at about 10% off; the exact figure is shown after you verify.

Because the military lane isn’t always cheapest, compare it against a prepaid “Pay Now” rate and any Costco/USAA/AAA rate.

Reported savings are around $10 off an adult ticket and ~$4 off a child ticket, though the venue quotes the rate by phone rather than a fixed public percentage. Call with your military ID ready and compare against area military-appreciation promos.

- [Firestone Complete Auto Care military & veteran discount (10% + tax-free, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/firestone): Firestone Complete Auto Care gives a real, year-round military discount: 10% off PLUS tax-free on tires and service, in-store, for active duty, veterans, reserves, Guard, retirees, and DoD/government ID holders with proof of service. The tax-free perk is the quiet standout — in a high-tax state it is worth ~8-10% on its own, so the everyday 10% + tax-free often beats a headline 15% that is still taxed.
- [Fjällräven military & veteran discount (No standard discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/fjallraven): Fjällräven has no standard military discount — no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID offer and no military promo code. Its only service-linked path is the application-based Industry Pro Program, whose eligible categories include military (active duty, reserves, veterans) and first responders, but which requires proof of full-time employment, takes 4–6 weeks to review, and does not publish its discount percentage.
- [Fleet Farm military & veteran discount (10–15% (event only), verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/fleet-farm): Fleet Farm has no standing, year-round military discount. What it runs are in-store military appreciation events around Veterans Day and Memorial Day, when veterans and active-duty members who show a military ID at the register get an extra 10–15% off (15% for Veterans Day 2025; 10% for Memorial Day). There is no online code and no verified SheerID sign-up.
- [Fleet Feet military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/fleet-feet): Fleet Feet offers a 10% military and law-enforcement discount on full-priced items, redeemed in-store with a valid Military, EMS, or Peace Officer ID. Because Fleet Feet is franchised, the program runs store-by-store — participation and accepted IDs are set locally, and there is no chain-wide corporate terms page. A last-season clearance pair often saves more, and the 10% can’t stack on sale prices.
- [Floor & Decor military & veteran discount (Event-only discounts, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/floor-and-decor): Floor & Decor has no everyday military discount — its official policy is occasional in-store military discount events (historically a limited-time 10%, once capped at $200 off, around Veterans Day), announced through its email list. The everyday 10% military discount in this category lives at Lowe’s (uncapped) and Home Depot ($400/yr cap) instead.

- [FootJoy military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/footjoy): FootJoy does not offer a military or veteran discount. There is no program on footjoy.com, and ID.me confirms it is "not aware that FootJoy offers Military discounts" — so there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID path either. Service members save the same way everyone does: the Semi-Annual Sale/outlet, a working public promo code, free FJ Insider shipping, and ID.me Shop cashback (~2.5%, open to all).

- [OGIO military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ogio): OGIO gives verified US military members — active duty, veterans, reservists, and retirees — 15% off their entire order at OGIO.com, verified through ID.me at checkout, with the same 15% extended to nurses, first responders, and teachers.
- [OOFOS military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/oofos): OOFOS offers 20% off plus free shipping over $75 for military and other eligible groups, verified through ID.me.
- [Oakley military & veteran discount (Member pricing via Oakley Standard Issue, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/oakley): Oakley’s real military benefit is Oakley Standard Issue (OSI) — a free membership at oakleysi.com for verified U.S. military, first responders, and government, with built-in member pricing (the ID.me storefront advertises “up to 50% off select styles, plus an extra 15% and free shipping”). The savings are baked into SI pricing, not shown as a code at checkout. The separate Oakley.com 15% via ID.me is for nurses, teachers, medical providers, and hospital employees — not military.
- [Office Depot / OfficeMax military & veteran discount (20% off in-store, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/office-depot): Office Depot and OfficeMax give veterans, active-duty and retired military, reservists, and their dependents 20% off qualifying regular-price purchases in stores nationwide — shown with ID at the register. Online, a separate Teacher/Military offer via ID.me pays 25% back in Bonus Rewards (store credit), not 25% off at checkout.
- [Old Navy military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/old-navy): Old Navy offers a 10% military discount on in-store purchases to active-duty, retired, and Reserve/Guard service members and their families — shown by presenting a valid, current military ID at the register. It is in store only and is not valid at Oldnavy.com.
- [Olight military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/olight): Olight offers a 10% military and veteran discount for verified U.S. members, done online through BeansID and applied while logged in at olight.com. It applies to full-price items only — it can’t be combined with any coupon or promo code and excludes flash-sale items, Members Area products, free bundles, and blind boxes, which is where Olight’s deepest prices usually live.
- [Olive Garden military & veteran discount (No everyday discount, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/olive-garden): Olive Garden does not offer an everyday military or veteran discount — its FAQ states it does not give a discount to any one group of guests, and it has no rewards program. The one confirmed military offer is a Veterans Day free entrée for dine-in veterans and active-duty members (special menu, show proof of service).
- [OluKai military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/olukai): OluKai offers a verified 10% military discount on your entire order (with a $60 minimum) at olukai.com, unlocked through free GovX verification for military, first responders, teachers, and government employees.
- [Omaha Steaks military & veteran discount ($10 off $79+, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/omaha-steaks): Omaha Steaks offers a real, official military discount: a flat $10 off any order of $79 or more, verified through ID.me for active-duty, veterans, retirees, reservists, and military spouses and dependents. It works on omahasteaks.com, the mobile app, and participating retail — but it cannot be combined with any other offer or discount, and Omaha Steaks’ constant package sales plus stackable public promo codes usually save more than $10.
- [Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo & Aquarium military & veteran discount (~10% off tickets, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/omaha-zoo): Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo & Aquarium publishes a discounted military admission price year-round — about 10% off standard adult and child gate rates — and gives free gate admission on Veterans Day (Nov 11) to active/retired military, veterans, and their immediate families.
- [On military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/on-cloud): On — the Swiss brand behind the "Cloud" running shoes — gives verified military members a community discount through ID.me. On publishes no percentage and defers to ID.me, which lists 15% off for U.S. and Canadian military; the value is set via ID.me and can change.
- [On (On Cloud) military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/oncloud): On gives verified U.S. and Canadian military 15% off via ID.me — issued as a single-use code and redeemable online only on On.com or the On app.
- [OnStar military & veteran discount (No subscription discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/onstar): OnStar publishes no standalone military or veteran discount on its Connected Services subscription plans, and there is no ID.me path at checkout. The real savings are the complimentary OnStar trial that ships with a new GM vehicle, choosing the lowest tier that meets your need, and retention/promo pricing — plus GM’s separate Military Appreciation discount on buying or leasing a new GM vehicle.
- [OpticsPlanet military & veteran discount (Up to 25% off, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/opticsplanet): OpticsPlanet offers a service discount of up to 25% off select brands for active-duty military, veterans, first responders, and healthcare workers — redeemed by phone, not online.
- [Origin USA military & veteran discount (GovX discount, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/origin): Origin USA offers its military and veteran discount through GovX. Verify your status and the discount applies to regular-priced items; the exact percentage is shown only after you verify. There is no ID.me path and no live on-site "veteran code."
- [Orvis military & veteran discount (10% via WeSalute+, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/orvis): Orvis offers 10% off select full-price apparel and dog gear per WeSalute’s terms — online only at orvis.com and exclusively for paid WeSalute+ members ($59.95 the first year) — and as of July 13, 2026 WeSalute flags the benefit as "currently being updated by the partner," while the free public 15% email welcome code beats the 10% outright.

- [OtterBox military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/otterbox): OtterBox publishes no first-party military discount and runs no ID.me offer — verified shoppers save most through GovX, ExpertVoice, or tax-free at the military exchange.
- [Our Place military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/our-place): Our Place gives verified military members and veterans 10% off orders of $100 or more at fromourplace.com through ID.me — but it can’t be combined with any other offer, and Our Place’s frequent 25–40% sitewide sales usually beat it.
- [Oura military & veteran discount (Up to 25% off (GOVX), verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/oura-ring): Oura runs two verified-savings programs: military, veterans, and first responders save through GOVX (Oura’s announcement describes up to 25% off), while students, educators, and healthcare professionals save a flat 10% on Oura Ring 4 and Oura Ring 4 Ceramic via ID.me.
- [Outback Steakhouse military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/outback): Outback Steakhouse offers a genuine everyday 10% "Heroes Discount" off your entire check, all day every day, for military veterans and servicemembers (plus their immediate family), police, firefighters, first responders, nurses, doctors and medical staff — verified by showing a valid ID in person, dine-in or by calling to order.
- [Outdoor Research military & veteran discount (Varies by status, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/outdoor-research): Outdoor Research runs no everyday military discount. Active-duty and reservists can apply to the discretionary Pro Program (discount depth unpublished), while veterans and retirees get a seasonal Veterans Day 25% promo via ID.me plus the GovX marketplace (up to ~40% off select styles) year-round.
- [Outer Banks Hotels & Rentals military & veteran discount (Varies by product, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/outer-banks-hotels): The Outer Banks is a destination, not a brand — so there is no single OBX military discount. Chain hotels (Hilton Garden Inn, Hampton, Holiday Inn Express, Comfort and others) honor their parent chain’s variable military/veteran rate; local vacation-rental companies give up to about 5% off full-week stays with a military ID; and the Armed Forces Vacation Club sells 7-night condo weeks at the Outer Banks Beach Club in Kill Devil Hills from roughly $369–$569.
- [Owala military & veteran discount (10% off (one-time), verified via VerifyPass)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/owala): Owala gives verified military members and veterans a one-time 10% off discount on its water bottles and drinkware, verified through VerifyPass, which emails a single-use code to enter at checkout on owalalife.com.
- [Owlet military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/owlet): Owlet does not offer a military discount — ID.me states it is not aware of any Owlet military offer, and owletcare.com publishes no military, veteran, nurse, or first-responder program. Military families still save two real ways: the Navy Exchange carries the Owlet Dream Sock Monitor tax-free for exchange-eligible shoppers, and Owlet discounts constantly in public — a 15% sitewide code was live when we checked, Black Friday 2025 took $100 off the Dream Sock, cashback portals pay 2–5%, and retailer listings mark the FDA-cleared Dream Sock HSA/FSA-eligible.
- [PGA TOUR Superstore military & veteran discount (10% in-store, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/pga-superstore): PGA TOUR Superstore gives active and retired military 10% off in stores only, with a valid military ID — but PING and Babolat are fully excluded and most premium club brands (Titleist, TaylorMade, Callaway, Mizuno and more) are excluded too. There is no online military discount.
- [PING military & veteran discount (Up to $30 rebate per club, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ping): PING doesn’t give a point-of-sale military discount — it runs a Military Rebate Program. Buy new, eligible PING clubs from an authorized US dealer, verify your service through ID.me, and claim a fixed-dollar virtual prepaid rebate card per club.
- [PODS military & veteran discount (Up to 10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/pods): PODS gives service members up to 10% off a move with promo code SERV10 — on local delivery and the first month’s storage, and on transportation for long-distance moves between PODS locations. Verify with ID.me or claim the code at booking.
- [POLYWOOD military & veteran discount (5% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/polywood): POLYWOOD offers a 5% military discount on polywood.com, verified for free through SheerID as a one-time code.
- [PUMA military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/puma): PUMA’s U.S. "Service Discount" gives qualified service members — military personnel, first responders, nurses, medical professionals, teachers, and government employees — 20% off their order on PUMA.com, verified through ID.me.

The real savings are public: near-constant sitewide sales up to 50% off (markdowns to 70%), PacSun Rewards (~4% back + $5 signup), the app-only APP20 extra 20%, and the UNiDAYS student 10% for college-enrolled dependents.

There’s no published military discount on single-visit general admission, and PacSci is not a 2026 Blue Star Museums participant.
- [Palmetto State Armory military & veteran discount (In-store only (discretionary), verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/palmetto-state-armory): Palmetto State Armory publishes no military or veteran discount online and uses no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID verification. Its retail stores are reported to honor a discretionary, unpublished in-store military discount when you show ID; online, the real savings path is Daily Deals / sale pricing stacked with a cashback portal (BeFrugal 7%, as of July 7, 2026).
- [Panda Express military & veteran discount (No official discount, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/panda-express): Panda Express has no official, company-wide military or veteran discount — it is not in the FAQ, rewards terms, or any corporate page, and Panda is absent from the major Veterans Day free-meal lists. Some individual locations grant a discretionary in-store "military courtesy" discount (commonly ~10%) with a valid ID, but it is not guaranteed and varies by store. The reliable savings is the free Panda Rewards program: a 25%-off welcome gift (up to $10), then points and monthly gifts.
- [Pandora military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/pandora): Pandora jewelry gives the verified military community 10% off through its Supporting Heroes program, verified by ID.me. After verifying, you get a single-use promo code valid 60 days, redeemable online at pandora.net or in-store at participating Pandora retailers (ID.me only). It’s limited to one code per customer per 24 hours, can’t be combined with other offers, and excludes 14K gold, Lab-Grown Diamonds, and gift cards. (This is the jewelry discount — not the unrelated Pandora music service’s 20% offer.)
- [Panera Bread military & veteran discount (No national discount, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/panera): Panera Bread has no national everyday military or veteran discount and no military verification provider. It runs a Veterans Day (Nov 11) freebie — a free bagel or bakery item plus a coffee — at participating locations only, largely through its franchisee Covelli Enterprises. Any everyday discount is a café’s discretionary courtesy and is never guaranteed.
- [Papa Johns military & veteran discount (No national military rate, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/papa-johns): Papa John’s has no official, nationwide military discount and no standing national military code — any military savings are local franchise or on-base/MWR deals that vary by store. The most reliable savings for everyone are the public 40–50% off app and site codes plus the free Papa Rewards program (75 points = $10 toward food).

Everyone, including service members, saves through year-round Web Specials and used gear via Worn Wear.

It is a promotional price, not a permanent rate: after 12 months it auto-renews at $10.99/month (or then-current retail) plus tax, and annual SheerID re-verification is required to keep the discount.

- [PenFed Credit Union military & veteran discount ($95 fee waived + 2% cash back, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/penfed): PenFed has no coupon-style military discount — and despite the name, anyone can join (open charter since its January 1, 2019 merger with Progressive Credit Union). The military benefit is Honors Advantage, a membership program on two cards: it waives the Pathfinder Rewards Visa Signature’s $95 annual fee, boosts Pathfinder earning to 4X on travel and 3X on dining (vs 3X/2X), and bumps the $0-fee Power Cash card to a flat 2% cash back (vs 1.5%). It applies automatically to active duty, Guard, Reserve, honorably discharged veterans, and military retirees — for life, because it’s a membership perk, not an SCRA/MLA legal requirement that ends with active duty. Civilians (and military spouses, who aren’t listed in the military route) get identical terms by holding a qualifying PenFed checking account. PenFed verifies status in its own application flow — no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX.

It also honors the discount via WeSalute+, and runs a dedicated military move call center (1-844-4TROOPS) for PPM/PCS moves.

Both are verified in person by showing ID to a Services associate — no ID.me/GovX/SheerID and no online redemption. Coupon-site "10–25% off via ID.me" claims are inaccurate.
- [Petco military & veteran discount (10% via GovX gift cards, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/petco): Petco has no official military or veteran discount in 2026 — no program on petco.com, no in-store policy, and ID.me says it’s "not aware of Petco offering Military community discounts." The one verified military-community path is GovX: members buy Petco digital gift cards at 10% off and spend them online or in-store on anything, including sale items. The verified everyday savings stack needs no military ID: Deals-menu pricing, paid with a discounted gift card, inside Hut Rewards.

- [PlayStation military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/playstation): PlayStation (Sony Interactive Entertainment) has no official military or veteran discount on the PS5, PS5 Pro, controllers, or PlayStation Plus. That is a DoD benefit gated by a DoD eligibility check, not a rate you unlock at priceline.com. For everyone, Priceline’s everyday savings are its free VIP program and Express Deals.

The same 5% extends to first responders, healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses, medical staff, hospital employees), and educational workers (teachers/school staff). It is a state mandate, not a Progressive program, and does not exist in the other 49 states.

The genuinely military-specific benefit is statutory: SCRA protection against lien sale of your belongings and penalty-free lease termination on deployment or PCS.

There is no flat percentage and no military coupon code.
- [Quince military & veteran discount (10% off first order, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/quince): Quince gives verified U.S. military members, first responders, nurses, and educators 10% off their first purchase through ID.me — a one-time, new-customer offer with a $40 minimum, applied via an auto-applied code at checkout on quince.com.
- [REEF military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/reef): REEF has no military discount on reef.com — no ID.me or SheerID checkout, and ID.me Shop says it is not aware of any REEF military offer. The military-specific routes that do exist are substitutes: a GovX storefront with gated member pricing, and tax-free Samsonite purchases at the military exchanges (AAFES and the Navy Exchange). For most shoppers, Samsonite’s deep public sales (advertised up to ~40% off) plus 2.5% Rakuten cash back is the winning path.

It is program pricing that varies by item, not a flat 30%, verified through a Samsung Account with ID.me (or a .mil/.gov/.edu/.company email); veterans and family route via WeSalute.

SeatGeek does NOT publish the amount, and it’s typically for your first purchase, one-time use, and may apply only to eligible events and listings. "Starlink military discount" claims online are third-party (an installer’s labor discount, or GovX accessory pricing) — not from Starlink. Starshield is a separate defense procurement channel, not a consumer discount.
- [Starz military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/starz): Starz publishes no military or veteran discount and uses no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute verification. The real savings are Starz’s recurring public intro promos, the cheaper annual plan, binge-and-cancel, and platform add-on pricing — all open to everyone.
- [State & Liberty military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/state-and-liberty): State & Liberty offers a standing 15% discount to active, reservist, veteran, and retired military personnel, verified through ID.me at online checkout — and because the brand runs no sales, it’s genuinely the best price you’ll get.
- [State Farm military & veteran discount (No national military rate, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/state-farm): State Farm has no nationwide military or veteran discount — none appears among the programs on its official auto discounts page. The only exception is Louisiana, where state law mandates a Military Personnel Discount for active-duty members and active Louisiana Air/Army National Guard reservists. Everywhere else, the real savings are Drive Safe & Save plus bundling — and a USAA or GEICO military quote before you renew.

The "10% via ID.me" on coupon sites is fabricated. The real military route to a discounted Stetson is Boot Barn, an authorized Stetson retailer, where ID.me-verified military and first responders get 10% off full-priced styles every day; on stetson.com itself, the end-of-season sale (40% off when live) is the deepest real discount.

Service members save the same way anyone does: catch an occasional public promo code and stack a cashback portal on top.

"Up to 20%" means only select grills get the full 20% — verify the model in-cart.

Current and former U.S. Military, military spouses and dependents, and first responders qualify.
