- [WeatherTech military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/weathertech): WeatherTech does not offer a military or veteran discount — its official FAQ states "We do not currently offer a military discount," and it does not honor third-party coupon-site codes. There is no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or WeSalute program. The only built-in way to save is WeatherTech’s shipping offer: spend $100+ for 50% off Ground Shipping or $250+ for free Ground Shipping.
- [Weber military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/weber): Weber gives verified military members 10% off at weber.com, verified through ID.me at checkout. The discount is weber.com-only — retail stores set their own policies — and it does not combine with promo codes, so Weber’s own public sales (or the tax-free military Exchange) can beat it.
- [Wendy's military & veteran discount ($3 off $20+ (WeSalute), verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wendys): Wendy's has no everyday automatic percentage military discount. Through its WeSalute partnership, verified service members and veterans get a recurring $3 off a $20+ My Wendy's app order, WendyMail holiday coupons, and a free Veterans Day breakfast combo.
- [West Elm military & veteran discount (No confirmable military rate, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/west-elm): West Elm has no confirmable military, veteran, or first-responder discount today — the "15% via SheerID" figure is legacy and unverifiable (ID.me is "not aware," West Elm isn’t on SheerID’s 2026 list, and sibling Pottery Barn’s 15% was discontinued). The real savings for everyone are the free The Key Rewards (2% / up to 10% carded) and West Elm’s frequent deep sitewide sales.
- [West Marine military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/west-marine): West Marine publishes no military, veteran, or first-responder discount and runs no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX military-verification flow. The honest way to save is timing a sitewide sale, joining free West Advantage Rewards, and layering a cash-back portal — plus, for active duty, the free BoatUS membership.
- [Whirlpool military & veteran discount (Member pricing via SheerID, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/whirlpool): Whirlpool offers an official military and veteran discount sitewide on major appliances at whirlpool.com, verified through SheerID — the percentage isn’t published on the page and appears in your account only after you sign in and verify.
- [Wiley X military & veteran discount (30% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wiley-x): Wiley X gives military, veterans, first responders, nurses, and government employees 30% off at wileyx.com, verified through ID.me.
- [Williams Sonoma military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/williams-sonoma): Williams Sonoma does not run a first-party military or veteran discount and there is no military code at checkout — it discontinued its old 15% in-store military discount in 2021. The real ways for service members to save are the free Key Rewards program, the deep Outlet / Open Box clearance, and public sales.
- [Wilson military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wilson): Wilson offers a 15% military discount on eligible merchandise for active, reserve, and retired military and their families, verified through SheerID and applied automatically at wilson.com — no code needed.
- [Windsor military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/windsor): Windsor gives active-duty military members and their spouses 10% off regular-priced items — in store only, by showing a valid military ID at the register. There is no online military discount, and veterans are not named as eligible.
- [Wingstop military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wingstop): Wingstop has no official military or veteran discount — nothing on its FAQ or offers pages, no verification partner, and ID.me confirms it isn’t aware of any Wingstop military program. Anything at the counter is a location-discretionary franchise courtesy. The verified savings path for everyone: join Club Wingstop (5 free boneless wings on signup) and order direct on wingstop.com or the app.
- [WonderWorks military & veteran discount (Free during Armed Forces Week, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wonderworks): WonderWorks has no standing, chain-wide published military discount, but during Armed Forces Week (about May 9–16) active-duty and retired military get FREE All Access admission at the door at Orlando and Myrtle Beach (guests $3 off each). Some locations, notably Pigeon Forge, also give ~$3 off in-store with a military ID — discretionary and varies.
- [Wrangler military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wrangler): Wrangler offers a 10% military discount online at wrangler.com, verified through ID.me and applied at checkout.
- [Wyndham Hotels & Resorts military & veteran discount (15%+ off (SML), verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/wyndham): Wyndham offers a genuine military discount with two paths. The everyday version is the Military Appreciation Rate — at least 15% off a hotel’s Standard Rate, booked with rate code SML on Wyndham’s own channels and verified by showing a military ID at check-in (no Rewards membership needed). Confirming your military status online via ID.me also unlocks an automatic GOLD tier upgrade, 3,000 bonus points after a qualifying stay, and an ID.me rate of up to 20% off the Best Available Rate. Compare SML against the ID.me rate for your dates and book the lower.
- [Xbox military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/xbox): There is no Xbox military discount. Microsoft runs a 10% military discount on the Microsoft Store, but its own terms exclude Xbox consoles, games, and accessories — and all subscriptions, including Xbox Game Pass. The 10% covers select consumer Surface devices and accessories only, verified through Microsoft's own eligibility check rather than ID.me.
- [Xfinity military & veteran discount (Military perks bundle, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/xfinity): Xfinity’s military offer is a perks bundle, not a percentage off: verified service members and military families with Xfinity Internet can get a free Xfinity Mobile line for 2 years, an instant upgrade to Diamond membership (including Peacock Premium at no extra cost), and NOW TV free for 1 year.
- [YETI military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/yeti): YETI offers a 20% military and veteran discount on eligible items, verified for free through ID.me.
- [YMCA military & veteran discount (Free via DoD program, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ymca): There is no single national YMCA military discount — each of the ~800 local associations sets its own rates, and military/veteran discounts (documented 10–20% off dues plus join-fee waivers) exist at some Ys and not others. The big national benefit is the DoD Military Outreach Initiative: a completely free YMCA membership plus free respite child care for eligible Title 10 members and families — with veterans, retirees, and Title 32 Guard explicitly excluded by the program’s own rules.
- [YNAB military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ynab): YNAB offers no military, veteran, or active-duty discount — no ID.me or SheerID verification and no military rate. The real savings paths are the 34-day free trial, the $109 annual plan, and a free year for enrolled college students.
- [Yakima military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/yakima): Yakima does not offer a military or veteran discount — there is no ID.me, GovX, SheerID, or VerifyPass program and no veteran tier at checkout. Service members save the same way everyone does: by timing Yakima’s recurring 20%-off sitewide sale (or a 25%-off bike-rack sale), buying from the "Deep Discount" clearance (up to ~40% off), and taking free shipping on orders $499+.
- [Yard House military & veteran discount (Free Veterans Day appetizer, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/yard-house): Yard House has no everyday, company-wide military or veteran discount. Its one official military offer is a free appetizer on Veterans Day (November 11) for veterans and active-duty service members, dine-in only. The best everyday savings are non-military: daily Happy Hour and discounted Darden gift cards.
- [YouTube Music military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/youtube-music): Neither YouTube Music Premium nor YouTube Premium has a military or veteran discount — service members pay standard rates. The real savings are the SheerID student plan ($8.99/mo), the family plan ($26.99/mo for up to 6), and the annual plan ($159.99/yr). The military ID.me offer people search for belongs to the separate YouTube TV product.
- [YouTube Premium military & veteran discount (No Premium discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/youtube-premium): YouTube Premium does not offer a military or veteran discount. Google’s help docs list only one discounted membership tier — the student plan, verified via SheerID — with no military/veteran/first-responder/medical/teacher tier. The military discount people search for belongs to a different product: YouTube TV (ID.me), with a separate ID.me offer for NFL Sunday Ticket. Those are alternatives, not a YouTube Premium discount.
- [YouTube TV military & veteran discount ($15/mo off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/youtube-tv): YouTube TV’s Base Plan is $67.99/mo for your first 12 months — $15/mo off the ~$82.99 standard price, about $180 saved over the year — for verified military, veterans, first responders, the medical community, and teachers via ID.me, redeemable through June 30, 2026. (Ignore the “no military discount” and stale “$69” claims.) After 12 months it reverts to full price. NFL Sunday Ticket has its own, separate military offer: $198 for the 2026 season (+$42 for RedZone) through Jan 10, 2027.
- [ZAGG military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/zagg): ZAGG offers no U.S. military or veteran discount — ID.me itself says it’s not aware of one. The real deal is ZAGG’s public buy-2 bundle (20–30% off) or 20% email-signup code, open to everyone.
- [Zales military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/zales): Zales offers verified military community members 10% off eligible jewelry, confirmed on Zales’s own website and verified through ID.me — redeemable online at zales.com and in-store.
- [Zappos military & veteran discount (No verified discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/zappos): As of June 23, 2026, Zappos has no military or veteran discount confirmable on a current Zappos source. Its former SheerID "Programs" discount (10% off for military, students, and teachers) has been discontinued. Service members get the same free shipping, free 365-day returns, and general savings as everyone.
- [Zara military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/zara): Zara offers no military, veteran, or first-responder discount; the real ways to save are its year-round Special Prices, twice-yearly sales, and (for students) a Student Beans code.
- [Zenni Optical military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/zenni): Zenni Optical gives a 10% military discount on all purchases, verified through ID.me — but it overrides all other codes and sales and can’t be combined with them.
- [ZooTampa military & veteran discount (Free summer admission, verified via In-store ID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/tampa-zoo): Through September 7, 2026, active-duty military get free ZooTampa admission plus up to three dependents with a valid military ID at the gate; year-round, active duty, retirees, and veterans get a reported $4 off per ticket (up to four).
- [Zumiez military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/zumiez): Zumiez publishes no military or veteran discount, and by the company’s own statement it does not issue coupons or promo codes at all — so there is no code to enter at checkout. Service members save instead by buying the same brands tax-free at the military Exchange when stocked, shopping Zumiez’s daily sale and clearance, taking the email free-shipping offer, and joining the free Stash loyalty program.
- [adidas military & veteran discount (30% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/adidas): adidas offers a 30% discount to verified military members, first responders, teachers, nurses, medical providers, hospital employees, and seniors 65+ through its "Home Team Heroes" program — verified free through ID.me and redeemable online, in store, and at factory outlets.
- [dbrand military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/dbrand): dbrand offers no military or veteran discount — no ID.me or SheerID verification and no "military code" at checkout. The only real way to save is the same public sitewide sale everyone gets.
- [discovery+ military & veteran discount (Ended June 2023, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/discovery-plus): discovery+ closed its military discount — 40% off the Ad-Lite plan, verified through SheerID — to new subscribers on June 1, 2023. Members who enrolled before that date are grandfathered and keep the rate only while they stay continuously subscribed; there is no way for new service members to sign up for it today.
- [eBay military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ebay): eBay does not offer its own military or veteran discount — it is a marketplace where sellers set prices, and eBay runs no ID.me, SheerID, or GovX military checkout. The only military-tagged offer is a third-party cash-back deal (up to about 2%) through ID.me Shop, ID.me’s cashback portal. The real savings are structural: eBay Certified Refurbished (a free 2-year Allstate warranty), seller “Make an Offer,” periodic site-wide coupons, and the tax-free military exchange for comparable new items.
- [etrailer military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/etrailer): etrailer offers no military or veteran discount and has no ID.me/GovX gate — its stated position is that it already prices low for every customer. The real savings are its everyday low pricing, deals/clearance page, and free-shipping thresholds.
- [eufy military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/eufy): eufy offers an official 20% military and first-responder discount at eufy.com, verified free through GovX ID as a single-use code — though its frequent deep sales often beat it.
- [evo military & veteran discount (10% off, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/evo): evo offers a 10% military discount on full-priced, eligible items for verified service members — but it excludes sale items, bikes, and surf gear, and often loses to evo’s public sales.
- [goodr military & veteran discount (No military discount, verified via Other)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/goodr): goodr runs no military or veteran discount on goodr.com — there is no ID.me, GovX, or SheerID step at checkout, and no first-responder, nurse, teacher, or student program. The honest ways to save are ExpertVoice (a verified pro deal for eligible service members), goodr’s frequent 20–25% sitewide sales that apply to everyone with no code, and Scheels’ 5% everyday military discount on the goodr it stocks.
- [iFIT military & veteran discount (5% off (NordicTrack), verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/ifit): There is no umbrella "iFIT military discount." iFIT is the app that runs on NordicTrack, ProForm, and FreeMotion machines, and only NordicTrack publishes a military discount — 5% off your entire order for current and former U.S. military, verified through GovX ID. ProForm offers no military discount, and the iFIT app subscription has no military price.
- [johnnie-O military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/johnnie-o): johnnie-O offers a verified 15% discount through GovX for military members, first responders, healthcare workers, government employees, and teachers — the only service discount the brand publishes.
- [lululemon military & veteran discount (15% off, verified via SheerID)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/lululemon): lululemon gives verified military members and first responders 15% off regular-price gear — including We Made Too Much, lululemon lab, and selfcare — verified through SheerID and redeemable online or in store.
- [melin military & veteran discount (30% off, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/melin): melin offers a 30% military and first-responder discount on full-price headwear at melin.com, verified through GovX for military, veterans, military family, first responders, medical, government employees, and teachers.
- [onX military & veteran discount (50% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/onx): onX gives verified current and former U.S. military members 50% off onX Hunt, onX Offroad, and onX Backcountry map memberships — applied through ID.me at checkout on onX’s website, on new purchases only. First responders, government employees, and students get 40%.
- [prAna military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/prana): prAna offers a 20% discount on full-priced items, plus free shipping, to verified military members — and the same 20% to first responders, nurses, medical workers, teachers, students, and government employees — verified free through ID.me.
- [tonies military & veteran discount (20% off, verified via ID.me)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/tonies): tonies gives verified members of the military community 20% off all purchases on us.tonies.com through its "Everyday Heroes" program — verified free through ID.me at checkout, with the same 20% for teachers, nurses, and healthcare workers.
- [xTool military & veteran discount (5% off, verified via VerifyPass)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/xtool): xTool offers 5% off to verified military members, veterans, first responders, government and healthcare workers, teachers, and students — verified through VerifyPass. The under-appreciated lever for machine owners is xTool’s Trade Up program ($50–$800 credit).
- [’47 Brand military & veteran discount (No brand-direct discount, verified via GovX)](https://www.navyweek.org/discount/47-brand): ’47 runs no brand-direct military discount — ID.me confirms it. The real military channel is GovX, where ’47 caps and apparel sell at member pricing. On 47brand.com, the everyday levers are the 15% first-order email code and the ’47 Family loyalty program (free shipping, early sale access).

## Fleet Week city guides

- [U.S. Fleet Week guide, city by city](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek): an
  independent, editorially maintained guide to U.S. fleet weeks and Navy
  maritime events — schedules, air shows, parade of ships, ship tours, and
  best free viewing spots. NavyWeek.org is not the organizer of any fleet
  week listed; each record links to the real organizing association.
- [SAIL250 Maryland 2026 (Jun 24–Jul 1, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/baltimore): The air-show leg of the 2026 tall-ship flotilla — SAIL250 Maryland filled Baltimore’s Inner Harbor with ships while jet teams flew over the Patapsco off Fort McHenry.
- [Sail Boston 2026 (Jul 11–16, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/boston): In the home port of USS Constitution, Sail Boston brings the America-250 tall-ship flotilla into Boston Harbor in July — a Grand Parade of Sail and free ship tours. No air show.
- [The Navy in Chicago 2026](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/chicago): No fleet week in Chicago — but the region is home to the Navy’s only boot camp and the WWII Lake Michigan training carriers. The August Air & Water Show is the lakefront’s spectacle.
- [Fleet Week Galveston 2026 (Apr 15–22, 2026 (concluded))](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/galveston): The Gulf-coast venue for Texas’ first fleet week — Galveston hosted the dawn Parade of Ships and the tours at Seawolf Park for Fleet Week Houston 2026 (same event).
- [Fleet Week Houston 2026 (Apr 15–22, 2026 (concluded))](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/houston): Texas’ first-ever fleet week — the inaugural Fleet Week Houston (April 2026) hosted USS Kearsarge and the fleet down the coast at Galveston for America’s 250th.
- [LA Fleet Week 2026 (May 22–25, 2026 (concluded))](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/los-angeles): Southern California’s Memorial Day kickoff to summer — free ship tours and a waterfront expo beside the museum Battleship IOWA in San Pedro. No air show.
- [Hyundai Air & Sea Show 2026 (May 23–24, 2026 (concluded))](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/miami): No ship-tour fleet week in South Florida — the Memorial Day Hyundai Air & Sea Show over Miami Beach, headlined by the Thunderbirds, is the region’s military spectacle.
- [SAIL250 New Orleans 2026 (May 27–Jun 1, 2026 (concluded))](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/new-orleans): New Orleans has no annual fleet week — but in 2026 the SAIL250 tall-ship flotilla visited the Mississippi riverfront for America’s 250th before sailing on to the East Coast.
- [Fleet Week New York 2026 (July 3–8, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/new-york): For America’s 250th, New York trades its Memorial Day Fleet Week for SAIL250 — a July 4 Parade of Sail up the Hudson, an international naval review, and a Blue Angels-led flyover over the harbor.
- [Sail250 Virginia 2026 (Jun 12–23, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/norfolk): At the world’s largest naval base, Hampton Roads hosted Sail250 Virginia in June 2026 — a Parade of Sail up the Elizabeth River, free ship tours, and a rare Naval Station Norfolk open house.
- [The Navy in Philadelphia 2026](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/philadelphia): No annual fleet week — but Philadelphia is the birthplace of the U.S. Navy and Marines, with the cruiser Olympia and submarine Becuna open year-round at Penn’s Landing.
- [Rose Festival Fleet Week 2026 (June 4–7, 2026 (concluded))](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/portland): One of the country’s oldest fleet weeks — U.S., Coast Guard, and Royal Canadian Navy ships sail up the Willamette, lift the downtown bridges, and open for free tours at the waterfront. No air show.
- [Fleet Week San Diego 2026 (November 6–15, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/san-diego): America’s original fleet week, in the country’s biggest Navy town — free ship tours at Broadway Pier and a Sea & Air Parade across San Diego Bay. (The Blue Angels fly the separate Miramar show.)
- [San Francisco Fleet Week 2026 (October 4–12, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/san-francisco): The West Coast’s biggest fleet week — Blue Angels over the bay, a Parade of Ships under the Golden Gate, and free ship tours along the Embarcadero.
- [Seafair Fleet Week 2026 (July 21 – August 2, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/fleetweek/seattle): Seattle’s summer classic — the Blue Angels over Lake Washington, a Parade of Ships into Elliott Bay, and free ship tours at Pier 46. Free from the lakeside parks; festival grounds ticketed.

## Jet team schedules (Blue Angels & Thunderbirds)

- [Blue Angels 2026 schedule](https://www.navyweek.org/blue-angels): the complete U.S. Navy
  Blue Angels 2026 tour — every city, date, and air show — with full city
  guides for published stops. NavyWeek.org is independent and not affiliated
  with the U.S. Navy or the squadron.
- [Thunderbirds 2026 schedule](https://www.navyweek.org/thunderbirds): the complete U.S. Air
  Force Thunderbirds 2026 tour — every city, date, and air show — with full
  city guides for published stops. NavyWeek.org is independent and not
  affiliated with the U.S. Air Force or the squadron.
- [Blue Angels Anchorage 2026 — Arctic Thunder Air Show & Open House](https://www.navyweek.org/blue-angels/anchorage): The Blue Angels headline Arctic Thunder at JBER — Alaska's biggest public event, free, with the Chugach Mountains as the show's back wall.
- [Blue Angels Annapolis 2026 — U.S. Naval Academy Air Show (Commissioning Week)](https://www.navyweek.org/blue-angels/annapolis): The Blue Angels fly over the Severn River for the U.S. Naval Academy's Commissioning Week — a free midweek, hometown-Navy tradition beside the Academy in Annapolis.
- [Thunderbirds Branson 2026 — Branson Air Show](https://www.navyweek.org/thunderbirds/branson): The Thunderbirds headline the Branson Air Show over Labor Day weekend — jet aerobatics over the Ozark ridgelines at the privately built Branson Airport.

## Military air show guides

- [Military air shows 2026 directory](https://www.navyweek.org/air-show): an
  independent, editorially maintained guide to the major U.S. military air shows
  — dates, free admission and ticket options, performers, parking, and gate
  rules, with a full visitor guide for each show. NavyWeek.org is not the
  organizer of any show listed; each guide links to the official source.
- [NAS Oceana Air Show 2026 (September 19–20, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/air-show/oceana): The U.S. Navy's largest open house at its East Coast Master Jet Base in Virginia Beach — September 19–20, 2026, headlined by the Blue Angels with free admission.
- [MCAS Miramar Air Show 2026 (September 25–27, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/air-show/miramar): The largest military air show in the U.S., headlined by the Blue Angels at MCAS Miramar in San Diego — September 25–27, 2026, with free admission and parking.
- [San Diego Air Show 2026 (September 25–27, 2026)](https://www.navyweek.org/air-show/san-diego): The "San Diego Air Show" is the MCAS Miramar Air Show — the largest military air show in the U.S., held September 25–27, 2026 with the Blue Angels and free admission.
- [Joint Base Andrews Air Show 2026 (2026 dates to be confirmed)](https://www.navyweek.org/air-show/andrews): The premier air show in the Nation’s Capital, at the home of Air Force One near Washington, DC — free admission, with the 2026 date updating as it’s announced.

## Guides

- [VA disability benefits (2026 pay rates, ratings, how to file)](https://www.navyweek.org/va-disability):
  long-form guide to U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs disability
  compensation. Authored by a U.S. Navy Reserve Captain.
- [Veterans Day 2026 (history, meaning, how the Navy observes it)](https://www.navyweek.org/veterans-day):
  guide to Veterans Day (Wednesday, November 11, 2026) — its origins as
  Armistice Day, how it differs from Memorial Day and Armed Forces Day, and
  the Flagstaff Navy Week (Nov 9–16) tie-in.
- [Veterans Day free meals 2026 (verified restaurant offers)](https://www.navyweek.org/veterans-day/free-meals):
  a primary-source-verified roundup of national restaurant chains offering a
  free meal or free food item to veterans and service members on November 11,
  2026. Every offer is checked against the brand's own official source and
  carries a visible "Verified" date; filterable by eligibility, dine-in vs.
  takeout, and nationwide vs. participating locations.
- [Veterans home care (VA benefits, eligibility, options)](https://www.navyweek.org/veterans-home-care):
  long-form guide to how the VA pays for in-home care — VA-arranged services
  vs. the Aid and Attendance pension, 2026 rates, who qualifies, how to apply,
  and how to pay a family member.
